abstract: The value of content cannot be realized until it is used. Every step in the production process that is not frictionless introduces an expense that incrementally reduces content's value. Though search in media asset management and production systems often receives a great amount of emphasis during discussion of digital workflows, we should remember the process of sharing media files between equipment and locations can be particularly expensive in terms of time and other resources. It often involves a significant number of manual steps to export, transfer, transcode, import, and re-link media with its associated metadata and context. Though users are now frequently expected to manually perform each step of this workflow, this process can and should be automated to the point of being invisible to the user. When implemented, this type of automation produces measurable gains in efficiency and content value in each workflow cycle. Because of the seamless nature of the resulting workflows, journalists are encouraged to use, share, and repurpose content more frequently, resulting in increased numbers of cycles, which multiply the effect.

authors.bio: Mike Palmer is the vice president and general manager of Masstech's News Division. His team received three major awards for innovation at NAB 2013 with Masstech for News—the first MAM system to deliver its core functionality for archive, search and restore through “video follows text” drag-and-drop workflows native to most NRCS systems. — Formerly the director of ENPS Design and Integration Strategy at Associated Press (AP), he led the evolution of its NRCS from a text-based system to one that allowed media of any type to be integrated into Newsroom workflows for broadcast or online distribution. Palmer is the former spokesperson for the MOS Protocol Group, an international industry organization, which he led for nearly 15 years. His work was recognized in 2001 with AP's Oliver Gramling Award for Achievement, in 2006, with Broadcasting and Cable's Technology Leadership Award, and in 2009 with a US Patent for media transmission.
